newsitem.title: USA: U.S., North Korea and South Korea to meet Monday. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S., North Korea and South Korea to meet Monday. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]

text.p: Senior officials from the United States, North Korea and South Korea will meet in New York on Monday in a new attempt to get peace talks for the divided peninsula going, the State Department announced on Wednesday.

Spokesman John Dinger (corrects from Glyn Davies) said Acting Assistant Secretary of State Charles Kartman would meet deputy foreign ministers from the two Koreas to discuss a U.S. proposal for four-party talks which would eventually also involve China.

The meeting, at a New York hotel, follows contacts among less senior officials from the three countries. "Clearly we wouldn't be meeting more senior North Korean officials if we did not feel talks were heading in the right direction," Dinger said.

He said Washington hoped that "ultimately -- it is difficult to predict exactly when -- that ultimately...we will realise four-party talks and ultimately peace on the Korean peninsula." That goal, he said "is, I would guess, quite a ways down the road." He had no further details about the content of the talks.

The four-nation talks, proposed by the United States and South Korea last year, aim to work out a peace settlement to replace a fraying armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War. Famine-threatened North Korea in April agreed in principle to join the peace talks but tied participation to large-scale food aid and an easing of U.S. trade sanctions.

Less senior U.S. and Korean negotiators met in New York a week ago, and U.S. officials said they were were "fine tuning" an announcement that would commit North Korea to attending a senior-level meeting that would set an agenda and other details for the peace talks.
